summary.headline: Planning Board releases six Ruby Estates lots, backs a $5,500 tree study, and grants occupancy extensions on Route 9.
summary.summary: The Southborough Planning Board took several formal actions on development and town planning items during its June 22, 2026 meeting. The board approved the release of six residential lots at the Ruby Estates subdivision after accepting a surety agreement, and authorized $5,500 for a consultant study to identify street tree planting sites. Members also recommended extending the temporary certificate of occupancy for 250 Turnpike Road and recommended final occupancy permits for Fresh Monkey and 200 Turnpike Road. Additionally, board members discussed a draft set of planning goals for the upcoming year and recognized longtime Open Space Preservation Commission member Freddie Gillespie following her departure from that board.

topics.title: 40-42 Central Street update
topics.summary: The chair briefly noted that there has been no progress on 40-42 Central Street since the previous meeting.
key_details: Address: 40-42 Central Street
No new updates or materials submitted

topics.title: 96 Mount Vickery Road (Ruby Estates) surety and lot release
topics.summary: The board reviewed a request from developer Bartolini Builders for 96 Mount Vickery Road (Ruby Estates), a six-lot subdivision originally permitted in 2021. Having installed utility infrastructure and roadway binder course for Lampson Drive, the developer submitted interim as-builts and executed a surety agreement covering a previously accepted bond of over $300,000. The board voted to accept the surety agreement and release all six lots from the subdivision covenant.
key_details: Location: 96 Mount Vickery Road (Lampson Drive)
Six-lot subdivision permitted in 2021
Bond estimate over $300,000 for remaining subdivision improvements
Town Counsel Jay Talerman reviewed the surety agreement
As-built review satisfied by Nitsch Engineering
topics.outcome: Surety agreement accepted and all six lots released from covenant
topics.why_it_matters: Releasing the subdivision covenant allows the developer to obtain building permits and sell lots for home construction.

topics.title: Hearing continuances: 22 and 154 Turnpike Road
topics.summary: Applicants for major site plan modifications at both 22 Turnpike Road (golf range) and 154 Turnpike Road requested continuances without testimony. The board voted to continue both hearings to its next regular meeting.
key_details: 22 Turnpike Road continued to July 13, 2026, at 6:45 PM
154 Turnpike Road continued to July 13, 2026, at 7:00 PM

topics.title: Subdivision regulations and zoning enforcement coordination
topics.summary: The board received a brief update on pending revisions to subdivision rules and regulations. Members also discussed scheduling a monthly coordination meeting on July 8 with the building commissioner and zoning administrator to review non-compliant site plans and monitor potential zoning amendments, such as signage along Route 9, accessory dwelling units, and short-term rentals.
key_details: First coordination meeting scheduled for July 8 with the building department
Staff is compiling a tracking spreadsheet of sites with outstanding site plan conditions
Topics for discussion include Route 9 signs, short-term rentals, and accessory dwelling unit bylaws
topics.outcome: Staff and board members will meet with the building department on July 8

topics.title: Street tree planting program proposal
topics.summary: The board discussed a proposal submitted by the tree warden from Davey Resource Group to launch an initial street tree planting plan. The $5,500 pilot study will evaluate 10 to 15 streets starting from the town center with low canopy cover and identify approximately 25 viable planting sites for future replacement trees. The board voted to approve the $5,500 expenditure and designated a board member to serve as liaison for long-term tree planning.
key_details: Consultant: Davey Resource Group
Cost: $5,500 from the tree fund
Scope: Study 10 to 15 streets and locate 25 potential tree planting sites
Addresses losses from National Grid removals and development projects
Board member designated as liaison to work with tree warden

topics.title: Planning Board FY27 draft goals
topics.summary: A board member presented a comprehensive draft outline of board goals and priorities for the upcoming year, modeled after similar documents used by other town boards. The draft addresses digital data migration to OneDrive, enforcement tracking, application streamlining, scenic roads, and implementation of Master Plan items. Board members were asked to submit edits through the town planner to comply with Open Meeting Law ahead of a full discussion on July 13.
key_details: Draft covers administration, regulatory modernization, zoning bylaws, open space, and communications
Includes goals derived from the 2021 Master Plan
Members instructed to channel feedback through the town planner to avoid serial deliberations

topics.title: 250 Turnpike Road temporary occupancy extension
topics.summary: Representative Georgeconn Banan of FD 250 Turnpike LLC requested a 90-day extension of the temporary certificate of occupancy for the Beehive Storage facility. Banan explained that because the access bridge over the wetlands has deteriorated, the applicant plans to install a dedicated septic system on the upper lot for the storage building and a separate system on the lower lot for the future contractor bays, rather than connecting across the bridge. The board voted to recommend that the building commissioner grant a 90-day extension.
key_details: Location: 250 Turnpike Road (Beehive Storage and contractor yard)
Current temporary certificate of occupancy recently expired
Applicant planning soil percolation testing with the Board of Health for separate upper-lot septic
Applicant plans future Approval Not Required (ANR) lot division and site plan modification
topics.outcome: Voted to recommend a 90-day extension of the temporary certificate of occupancy

topics.title: 118 Turnpike Road (Fresh Monkey) occupancy recommendation
topics.summary: The town planner reported that Fresh Monkey at 118 Turnpike Road, Suite 101, had submitted an engineer's certification letter verifying that all conditions of their change-of-use site plan approval were completed. The board voted to accept the engineer's letter and recommend the issuance of a full Certificate of Occupancy.
key_details: Business: Fresh Monkey, 118 Turnpike Road, Suite 101
Condition 8 satisfied by engineer certifying letter
topics.outcome: Voted to accept the engineer letter and recommend full Certificate of Occupancy

topics.title: Planner's report: 200 Turnpike Road bond and town updates
topics.summary: The town planner gave updates on several town projects. The board accepted a surety agreement for 200 Turnpike Road backed by a $30,000 bond for landscaping and voted to recommend a permanent occupancy permit. The planner also reported that St. Mark's Dormitory resolved outstanding landscaping items and is ready for a full occupancy permit, noted town meeting dates set by the Select Board, and mentioned a 5 percent compensation increase for town staff approved by the Personnel Board.
key_details: 200 Turnpike Road: $30,000 bond and surety agreement accepted for landscaping through October 2027
St. Mark's Dormitory: Minor landscaping corrections completed for full occupancy
Special Town Meeting scheduled for Saturday, October 17, 2026, at 10 AM
Annual Town Meeting scheduled for Saturday, March 20, 2027, at 10 AM
Zoning Board of Appeals hearing scheduled for July 15 on Pasqual variances for light poles and retaining walls
topics.outcome: Voted to accept the 200 Turnpike Road surety agreement and recommend full certificate of occupancy

topics.title: Routine business and tribute to Freddie Gillespie
topics.summary: The board approved the meeting minutes of June 1, 2026. The chair and members then paid tribute to Freddie Gillespie for her 26 years of service to the town and collaboration with the Planning Board after the Select Board opted not to reappoint her to the Open Space Preservation Commission.
key_details: Minutes of June 1, 2026 approved
Recognition of Freddie Gillespie for 26 years on the Open Space Preservation Commission
Next Planning Board meeting scheduled for July 13, 2026
